rows.fault_trigger: "The Double-Clutch". Attempting to make a dynamic football move or break up-field before the ball is completely secured in the hands, leading to direct drops or immediate bobble-fumbles upon first contact.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Instantly secure the ball out of the snap exchange or handoff fake and transition it directly to the body, completely avoiding any "double-clutch" or premature up-field break before the ball is fully possessed.

rows.fault_trigger: "Flagging" the Ball. Carrying the ball loosely away from the body while running in space. This heavily exposes the ball to trailing defenders punching or stripping it from behind.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hook the fingers over the front point, press the forearm along the seam, and clamp the back half of the football securely between the forearm and bicep.

rows.fault_trigger: Exposing the Breast. Carrying the football across the middle of the chest with a nose-up orientation. This allows a defender to punch it cleanly and violently out from the front.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Press the inner side of the football firmly against the rib cage with the nose tucked up beneath the armpit, completely locking the elbow to the torso to eliminate daylight.
Read interior pursuit and transfer the ball to the outside arm (closest to the sideline), freeing the inside arm to stiff-arm or guard against incoming tacklers.
The moment traffic closes in or a tackle is initiated, wrap the off-hand over the ball (two-handed carry) and chin the football to protect it completely through the ground.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the feet efficiently under the body — the step creating a stable base without excessive stride length or unnecessary movement.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a decisive first step in the designed direction while maintaining balance and preparing the throwing platform — creating proper throwing rhythm without drifting.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the one-step progression with proper timing from snap reception to throw — synchronized with the route concept.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the shotgun stance into the one-step throwing movement immediately after receiving the snap — quick, controlled, maintaining throwing posture without unnecessary gather steps.

Track both the hip-line rotation angle AND the lateral (horizontal) displacement of Pelvis Center over the same ~10-15 frame window. Coaching target: moderate rotation with a pronounced lateral displacement toward the rollout side. rows.fault_trigger: Carrying the Ball Low. Holding the ball down at your waist while sprinting out wide. Carrying the ball low lengthens your release time and increases the risk of a strip-fumble from a trailing defender.

NOTE: this reports a RELATIVE displacement rate only - an absolute speed figure needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) and a known frame rate; until then only relative comparisons (e.g. against this player's own top-speed baseline) are meaningful, not a universal threshold. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the ball tightly under your chin with both hands. Lean your shoulders forward and sprint horizontally toward the flat, using pure athletic speed to gain the edge on the defense.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Direct the Foot. Planting with your toe still pointed toward your deep drop track. This causes you to drift endlessly toward the sideline, completely shrinking your throwing window.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first. Square your torso toward the sideline or target path, settle your feet rapidly if the throw is deep, or deliver the ball cleanly while rolling at a full sprint.

rows.fault_trigger: Eyes tip the play or disrupt the exchange. (Eye gaze/discipline not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Appropriate eye discipline for the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange / tipping the play. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/discipline = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate eye discipline based on the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low or away from the torso approaching the exchange. (Ball position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure the ball with two hands — throwing hand back half, off-hand front half — tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; ball position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand secures the front — ball tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong shotgun depth relationship, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (~5 yards is a recommendation, not a calibrated threshold; absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative | GUN] Shotgun ~5 yds behind center — maintain the depth relationship to the LOS + RB path for timing/spacing/blocking angles. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale (~5 yds is a recommendation, not a threshold).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the shotgun alignment (roughly 5 yards behind the center), maintain the correct depth relationship to the line of scrimmage and the running back's path so timing, spacing, and blocking angles hold.

rows.fault_trigger: Not clearing the midline, opening with the wrong foot, toes not squared parallel to the line, or crossing/choppy steps that stop momentum or drift off the path. (The track's aiming point depends on the run concept, which is not captured — reported, not judged.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS MOTION | GUN] 'Step in the bucket' off the midline with the near foot, toes squared parallel to the LOS (basketball-defensive-stance base); efficient steps through the exchange. Step/open-angle + track measurable from pose; aiming point (run concept) deferred — report, don't judge.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Step off the midline ('step in the bucket') with the foot closest to the running back's side, squaring the toes parallel to the line of scrimmage into an athletic, basketball-defensive-stance base — efficient steps into and through the exchange with proper spacing, timing and balance, staying on the designed path. The toes align to the designated track for the called run (aiming point varies by concept).

rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.

rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)

rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.

rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.

rows.fault_trigger: Collapsing the mesh window, poor spacing or body position, or the ball not kept flat and secure into the mesh. (The running back securing the exchange needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | GUN] Maintain LOS spacing, ball flat + secure catch-to-hip for a prolonged mesh window, hold body position/balance. PROXY (solo) = spacing, ball-vs-body carriage, reach; the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the shotgun, reach the mesh maintaining proper spacing to the line of scrimmage, keeping the ball flat and secure and creating a prolonged mesh window (the ball riding from the catch back toward the hip) while holding body position and balance. (Camera judges the QB's own spacing, ball carriage relative to his body, and reach; the exchange itself needs the RB.)

rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled catch, hands not presented up, or an unbalanced entry into the exchange. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking; ~5 yards is a recommendation, not a threshold.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | GUN] ~5 yds behind center, athletic slightly-staggered base, hands up to catch a thrown snap (not butt-to-gut); timing/rhythm, balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the shotgun snap — aligned roughly 5 yards behind the center in an athletic, slightly-staggered base with the hands up, catching the ball thrown through the air (not a butt-to-gut exchange) — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor receiving posture.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Chest upright, hips loaded, spine neutral — athletic receiving posture. Pad level + posture measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Chest remains upright, hips loaded, and spine neutral while maintaining an athletic receiving posture.

rows.fault_trigger: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye tracking not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral while eyes track the anticipated snap location + defensive alignment. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE tracking = deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes track the anticipated snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep behind center, forcing a reach or drift for the snap. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] SHOTGUN depth: align at the prescribed depth behind center so the snap enters the center of the receiving window without reaching or drifting. Gun-specific row (under-center has no depth). Relative depth/alignment measurable; absolute needs a scale reference. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center while maintaining posture that allows the snap to enter the center of the receiving window without reaching or drifting.

rows.fault_trigger: Weight on the heels or unnecessary body movement during reception. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight balanced through mid-foot + balls of the feet for efficient reception without unnecessary body movement. Weight = proxy (ankle-over-mid-foot + stillness is the signal). Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight remains balanced through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, allowing efficient reception without unnecessary body movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow or too wide for balanced shotgun reception.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Balanced athletic base supporting clean shotgun reception + immediate movement after the catch. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet establish a balanced athletic base that supports clean shotgun reception and immediate movement after the catch.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — lower-body readiness immediately after the catch. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso to maintain lower-body readiness immediately after the catch.

rows.fault_trigger: Feet misaligned — poor balance during the catch/transition.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet aligned to support balance during the catch + efficient transition into the play. Foot alignment measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet remain aligned to support balance during the catch and efficient transition into the offensive play.

rows.fault_trigger: Knees locked or over-bent — loses explosive readiness.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knees slightly flexed — explosive movement immediately after securing the ball. Knee angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed, allowing explosive movement immediately after securing the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders not square to the LOS.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders square to the LOS — immediate transition into throwing/run/mesh mechanics. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain square to the line of scrimmage, allowing immediate transition into throwing, run, or mesh mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Hands too high/low/wide of the window, stiff wrists, or poor finger spread. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
pose_landmarks: Right Elbow. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] SHOTGUN receiving window: hands comfortably in front of the torso at the expected snap location; fingers naturally spread, thumbs relaxed, elbows slightly flexed, wrists soft to absorb the ball into the body. Hand POSITION = pose-measurable; FINGER/thumb detail = needs the Hand landmarker. Differs from under-center (in front, not under center). Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hands positioned comfortably in front of the torso at the expected snap location — fingers naturally spread with thumbs relaxed, elbows slightly flexed, and wrists soft to absorb the football cleanly into the body.

rows.fault_trigger: Reaching or excess foot movement disrupting accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet under the body during the transition — no reaching or excessive movement that disrupts accuracy. A 1 Step drop contains NO crossover. Foot placement measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet remain underneath the body during the transition — avoiding reaching or excessive movement that disrupts accuracy.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong depth relationship or inadequate throwing space. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Maintain the correct pistol relationship from center while the one-step movement creates proper throwing space. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain the correct pistol relationship from the center while allowing the one-step movement to create proper throwing space.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose or away from the chest after the snap. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure two-hand control after the pistol snap — ball protected against the chest before transitioning to throwing position. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand control after the pistol snap — the football stays protected against the chest before transitioning into throwing position.

rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed one-step progression out of sync with the route concept.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the one-step progression with correct timing from snap to throw — movement matches the route concept + offensive timing. A 1 Step drop contains NO crossover. Step timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the one-step progression with correct timing from snap reception to throw — movement matching the route concept and offensive timing.

rows.fault_trigger: Extra reset steps or hitch before delivery.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Immediate snap-to-throw rhythm — no additional reset steps or unnecessary movement before delivery. Tempo measurable (quick-game snap-to-throw). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain immediate snap-to-throw rhythm — no additional reset steps or unnecessary movement before delivery.

rows.fault_trigger: Drifting or off-balance first step disrupting throwing alignment.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled first step maintaining throwing rhythm, balance, lower-body readiness — proper alignment without drifting. First-step control/direction measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a controlled first step that maintains throwing rhythm while preserving balance and lower-body readiness — creating proper throwing alignment without drifting.

rows.fault_trigger: Head uncontrolled or eyes slow to the target. (Gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Visual discipline through the snap + movement — eyes transition quickly to the target, head controlled. Head orientation measurable; gaze deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain visual discipline through the snap and movement — eyes transition quickly to the target while the head remains controlled.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early through the snap transition/step.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders controlled through the snap transition + step — align to the target without opening early. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain controlled through the snap transition and step — aligning toward the target without opening early.

rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding or wrong step length for quick-game timing.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Appropriate step length for quick-game timing while maintaining balance + throwing posture. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use the appropriate step length for quick-game timing while maintaining balance and throwing posture.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded or drifting from under the torso before the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips loaded underneath the torso to support efficient lower-body rotation + throwing power. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded underneath the torso to support efficient lower-body rotation and throwing power.

rows.fault_trigger: Unnecessary gather steps or lost posture out of the pistol snap.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition from the pistol stance into the one-step movement immediately after the snap — maintain athletic posture, secure the ball, move efficiently, no unnecessary gather steps. Transition timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the pistol stance into the one-step movement immediately after receiving the snap — maintaining athletic posture, securing the football, and moving efficiently without unnecessary gather steps.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — needs a correction step before the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Balanced plant position after the one step — plant foot allows immediate throwing motion, no additional correction. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced plant position after the one step — the plant foot allows immediate throwing motion without additional correction.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide immediately after the step.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Balanced throwing base immediately after the step — feet under the body to support efficient release. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a balanced throwing base immediately after the step — feet underneath the body to support efficient release mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Off-balance or misaligned platform at release.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Finish with balanced feet, aligned hips + shoulders, proper weight transfer, immediate ability to deliver. The complete throwing platform measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Finish with balanced feet, aligned hips and shoulders, proper weight transfer, and immediate ability to deliver the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Head drops/bobs or eyes come down during the drop. (Gaze/reads not pose-measurable — deferred.) Head bouncing, dipping, or rocking through the drop; upper body unstable, degrading spatial awareness and balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Downfield vision throughout the drop while progressing through reads. Head orientation measurable; gaze/reads deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain downfield vision throughout the drop while progressing through defensive reads. Head stays stable and level over the spine throughout the drop — no bouncing, dipping, or rocking of the upper body, which costs spatial awareness and balance.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — feet drift or need extra steps before the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Proper plant foot position at the top of the drop — allows immediate transition into the throw. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish proper plant foot position at the top of the drop — allowing immediate transition into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Inconsistent or overstriding through the drop. Steps too long or too choppy, so the rhythm of the drop no longer matches the pass route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled stride length through the three-step drop while preserving balance + throwing posture. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain controlled stride length through the three-step drop while preserving balance and throwing posture. Stride length stays consistent and matched to the route’s timing — neither over-long nor choppy.

rows.fault_trigger: Pauses, drifts, or arrives early/late.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Smooth timing from snap through the final step — avoid pauses, drifting, or arriving early. Tempo/rhythm measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain smooth timing from snap reception through the final step — avoiding pauses, drifting, or arriving early.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.
rows.fault_trigger: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Knees crossing (karaoke-style) rather than the feet gliding past. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Weight shifting forward onto the front foot, preventing a clean load. Toes pointing backward or knees swinging wide off the linear path. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or wasted movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet glide low to the ground — low vertical oscillation of the ankles/hips, ground contact maintained, minimal heel contact. The ONE designed crossover is foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. The designed crossover step is a FOOT crossing past foot while the knees stay on a linear path; the knees do not cross over one another as in a karaoke drill. Base stays wide enough to hold balance and weight stays centred, not forward on the front foot.

rows.fault_trigger: Off-balance or shallow first step.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled first step creating proper depth while maintaining balance + readiness to throw. First-step control measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a controlled first step that creates proper depth while maintaining balance and readiness to throw.

rows.coaching_cue: Two hands on it — relaxed, not loose.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball drops off the chest or elbows flare during the drop. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.) Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position.
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand ball security throughout the drop — ball protected + positioned for efficient throwing transition. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand football security throughout the drop — the ball remains protected and positioned for efficient throwing transition. Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

rows.fault_trigger: Loses downhill posture or mistimes the transition into the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition from pistol stance into the three-step drop after securing the snap — maintain downhill posture while creating proper throwing rhythm. Transition timing + posture measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the pistol stance into the three-step drop after securing the snap — maintaining downhill posture while creating proper throwing rhythm.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips drift from under the torso or misalign for rotation. Back hip locked or tight through the crossover, preventing clean weight transfer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips under the torso + aligned for efficient rotation into the throw. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain underneath the torso and aligned for efficient rotation into the throw. Hips stay loose and mobile through the crossover so weight can transfer cleanly into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stable throwing base at the top of the drop with feet under the body. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a stable throwing base at the top of the drop with feet underneath the body.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong depth relationship, collapsing lanes or timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Maintain correct pistol depth relationship from center while completing the three-step drop — depth creates throwing lanes + maintains timing. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain the correct pistol depth relationship from the center while completing the three-step drop — the depth creates throwing lanes and maintains timing.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — stay low, don't bounce.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong step count or inconsistent rhythm/spacing. Crossover missing, or occurring on the wrong step (it belongs on the second). Steps too long or too choppy so the rhythm no longer matches the route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the three-step progression with consistent rhythm + spacing — maintain timing while preserving lower-body control. Contains ONE crossover, on the second step. Step count, crossover count + position, and rhythm all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the three-step progression with consistent rhythm and spacing — maintaining timing while preserving lower-body control. The drop contains ONE crossover step on the second step, turning the hips toward the target before the plant.

rows.fault_trigger: Finishes off-balance or not throwing-ready at the top of the drop. Weight stuck on the back foot at release, so the throw lacks ground force and becomes all arm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Finish with balanced feet, proper weight transfer, aligned hips + shoulders, ability to deliver immediately. The complete throwing platform measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Finish with balanced feet, proper weight transfer, aligned hips and shoulders, and the ability to deliver immediately. Weight transfers off the back foot into the throw, generating ground force rather than leaving the throw to the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early during the drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + controlled through the drop — avoid opening early before the throw. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and controlled through the drop — avoiding opening early before the throw. Shoulders stay level and controlled through the drop. The front shoulder neither collapses nor over-rotates — either turns the hips prematurely and blinds vision to one side.

rows.fault_trigger: Weak or off-balance first step that fails to create depth.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Strong first step initiating depth while maintaining balance + throwing posture. First-step drive measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a strong first step that initiates depth while maintaining balance and throwing posture.

rows.fault_trigger: Rushed, paused, or disconnected tempo through the steps.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent tempo through all five steps — smooth + connected to the throwing motion. Tempo/rhythm measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent tempo throughout all five steps — smooth and connected to the throwing motion.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — feet drift or unbalanced at the top.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Reach the top of the drop with correct plant foot location + balanced posture to transition into the throw. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the top of the drop with correct plant foot location and balanced posture to transition into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Inconsistent or overstriding through the progression. Steps too long or too choppy, so the rhythm of the drop no longer matches the pass route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent stride length throughout the five-step progression while preserving balance + throwing readiness. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent stride length throughout the five-step progression while preserving balance and throwing readiness. Stride length stays consistent and matched to the route’s timing — neither over-long nor choppy.

rows.fault_trigger: Drifts excessively deep or wrong depth relationship. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Maintain proper pistol depth relationship from center while reaching the required passing depth — create space without drifting excessively deep. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain proper pistol depth relationship from the center while reaching the required passing depth — creating space without drifting excessively deep.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — stay low, don't bounce.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong step count or inconsistent rhythm/spacing. Fewer or more than two crossovers, or crossovers on the wrong steps. Steps too long or too choppy so the rhythm no longer matches the route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the five-step progression with consistent rhythm, spacing, body control — maintain timing with deeper route concepts. Contains TWO crossovers. Step count, crossover count + position, and rhythm all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the five-step progression with consistent rhythm, spacing, and body control — maintaining timing with deeper route concepts. The drop contains TWO crossover steps, building depth before finishing on a balanced plant.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.
rows.fault_trigger: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Knees crossing (karaoke-style) rather than the feet gliding past. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Weight shifting forward onto the front foot, preventing a clean load. Toes pointing backward or knees swinging wide off the linear path. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or movement that disrupts timing.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet glide low to the ground — low vertical oscillation of the ankles/hips, ground contact maintained, minimal heel contact. The TWO designed crossovers are foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. The two designed crossover steps are FOOT crossing past foot while the knees stay on a linear path; the knees do not cross over one another as in a karaoke drill. Base stays wide enough to hold balance and weight stays centred, not forward on the front foot.

rows.coaching_cue: Two hands on it — relaxed, not loose.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball drops off the chest or elbows flare during the longer drop. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.) Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position.
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure two-hand football control throughout the longer drop — ball protected until the throwing motion. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand football control throughout the longer drop — the football remains protected until entering the throwing motion. Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stable throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet positioned for immediate release. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a stable throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet positioned for immediate release.

rows.fault_trigger: Unnecessary movement or lost posture transitioning into the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition smoothly from pistol stance into the five-step drop — secure the snap, maintain athletic posture, create depth without unnecessary movement. Transition timing + posture measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition smoothly from the pistol stance into the five-step drop — securing the snap, maintaining athletic posture, and creating depth without unnecessary movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or tilt during the drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + controlled throughout the drop while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and controlled throughout the drop while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulders stay level and controlled through the drop. The front shoulder neither collapses nor over-rotates — either turns the hips prematurely and blinds vision to one side.

rows.fault_trigger: Finishes off-balance or not throwing-ready at the top of the drop. Weight stuck on the back foot at release, so the throw lacks ground force and becomes all arm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Finish with a complete throwing platform — balanced feet, loaded hips, aligned shoulders, proper weight transfer, immediate throwing capability. Measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Finish with a complete throwing platform — balanced feet, loaded hips, aligned shoulders, proper weight transfer, and immediate throwing capability. Weight transfers off the back foot into the throw, generating ground force rather than leaving the throw to the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips drift from under the torso or misalign for power transfer. Back hip locked or tight through the crossover, preventing clean weight transfer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips under the torso + prepared to transfer power efficiently into the throw. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain underneath the torso and prepared to transfer power efficiently into the throw. Hips stay loose and mobile through the crossover so weight can transfer cleanly into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Head drops/bobs or eyes come down during the drop. (Gaze/reads not pose-measurable — deferred.) Head bouncing, dipping, or rocking through the drop; upper body unstable, degrading spatial awareness and balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Disciplined downfield vision throughout the drop while processing coverage + defensive movement. Head orientation measurable; gaze/reads deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain disciplined downfield vision throughout the drop while processing coverage and defensive movement. Head stays stable and level over the spine throughout the drop — no bouncing, dipping, or rocking of the upper body, which costs spatial awareness and balance.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line and hip-line should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, confirming a square, symmetric stance. NOTE: the stated alignment depth (e.g. 4.5-5 yards for Gun, 3-4 yards for Pistol) is NOT measurable from pose alone - it requires a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) or field-marking calibration. This signal checks squareness only, not depth.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align in a balanced, shoulder-width parallel stance 3 to 4 yards deep, directly on the mid-line of the formation.

rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly on the open-gate pivot that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a wide ~90-degree open-gate pivot, clearing the frame from the center-exchange space instantly. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap cleanly. Take an immediate, wide open-gate pivot step at a 90-degree angle toward your rollout side, instantly clearing your frame from the center-exchange space.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Sprint intensity proxy: horizontal (lateral) displacement of Pelvis Center per frame, tracked continuously through the sprint. Coaching target: sustained high displacement-per-frame with no deceleration, consistent with '100% sprint velocity.' NOTE: this reports a RELATIVE displacement rate only - an absolute speed figure needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) and a known frame rate; until then only relative comparisons (e.g. against this player's own top-speed baseline) are meaningful, not a universal threshold. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bring the ball tightly to your chest with both hands, drop your chin, and sprint horizontally at 100% velocity. Because there is no playaction fake, your only protection is outrunning the unblocked edge defender.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Point the Toe. Planting with your foot still pointed wide of the target path. You will slip, blow out your base, or delay your break, resulting in an inaccurate, off-balance throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: As you clear the tackle box, slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This compact step serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first to locate your targets. Square your shoulders to your throw, snap your wrist, and deliver the ball while moving downhill to maximize pass velocity.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line and hip-line should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, confirming a square, symmetric stance. NOTE: the stated alignment depth (e.g. 4.5-5 yards for Gun, 3-4 yards for Pistol) is NOT measurable from pose alone - it requires a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) or field-marking calibration. This signal checks squareness only, not depth.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align tightly 3 to 4 yards deep directly behind the center, with the running back stacked directly behind you. Establish a balanced, shoulder-width parallel stance.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a fast ~180-degree reverse-pivot, turning the back toward the line of scrimmage to generate a linear track for the running back. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Catch the snap and immediately execute a fast reverse-pivot to turn your back to the line of scrimmage, generating a linear downhill path for the stacked running back.

rows.fault_trigger: Standing Too Upright. Failing to bend at the waist during the linear handoff fake. Standing straight up exposes the empty ball to the linebackers, giving away the bootleg instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso flexion: angle between the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line and vertical, measured at the peak of the mesh point (side view). Coaching target: a clear forward bend at the waist, shielding the ball with the upper torso. NOTE: this measures torso BEND only, not 'vision committed to the mesh' - eye gaze is not pose-measurable, and head orientation is not a reliable substitute here since a bent-forward head position is ambiguous between watching the mesh and simply looking down. The coaching standard's real intent (linebackers can't read the fake) is only partially captured by this signal.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Stick the ball deep into the stomach of the running back as they charge directly downhill. Keep your head and eyes locked into the mesh, shielding the ball with your upper torso to sell a heavy interior run play.

rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding the Plant. Reaching too far forward to change direction out of the linear track. This locks up your hips and prevents you from getting your shoulders squared up to make an accurate throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Slip the ball out of the mesh late. Slam your outside foot down hard under your hips with the toe pulled up into sharp dorsiflexion. Instantly point your toe toward the perimeter to drive your body weight out of the linear track and onto a wide, looping rollout line.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first. Keep your front shoulder tucked, square your chest to the line of throw, and unleash the football with full velocity while clearing the edge.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low or away from the torso approaching the exchange. (Ball position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure the ball with two hands — throwing hand back half, off-hand front half — tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; ball position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand secures the front — ball tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase.

rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)

rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.

rows.fault_trigger: Eyes tip the play or disrupt the exchange. (Eye gaze/discipline not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Appropriate eye discipline for the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange / tipping the play. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/discipline = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate eye discipline based on the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to clear the center-to-tailback line, a loose or wide pattern instead of the tight two-step, or toes not aligned to the back's track. (The 45° / A-gap opening is illustrative of clearing the midline, not a fixed threshold; the aiming point depends on the run concept, which is not captured — reported, not judged.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS MOTION | PISTOL] Tight two-step pattern (e.g. ~45° into the A-gap, illustrative not a threshold) to clear the center-to-tailback line; toes parallel to the RB's track; controlled downhill steps. Step/open-angle + track measurable; aiming point (run concept) deferred — report, don't judge.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use a tight two-step footwork pattern (for example opening at roughly 45° into the A-gap) to clear entirely off the center-to-tailback straight line, aligning the toes parallel to the running back's incoming track — controlled, downhill-connected steps with proper spacing, timing and balance.

rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled catch, or an unbalanced entry that isn't ready for the downhill mesh. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking; ~3 yards is a recommendation, not a threshold.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | PISTOL] ~3 yds, upright to survey; clean catch preparing for the downhill mesh; timing/rhythm, balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the pistol snap — aligned closer to the line (roughly 3 yards) in an upright posture to survey the defense, catching the ball cleanly and preparing for the downhill mesh — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong pistol depth relationship, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (~3 yards is a recommendation, not a calibrated threshold; absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative | PISTOL] Pistol ~3 yds, upright — maintain the depth relationship so the deeper-aligned tailback's exchange keeps timing/spacing/blocking angles. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale (~3 yds is a recommendation, not a threshold).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the pistol alignment (closer to the line, roughly 3 yards, upright to survey the defense), maintain the correct depth relationship so the exchange with the deeper-aligned tailback keeps its timing, spacing, and blocking angles.

rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.

rows.fault_trigger: Losing the downhill track or the balanced base, or the ball not seated for the deeper tailback's straight path through the mesh. (The running back securing the exchange needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | PISTOL] Downhill mesh, balanced base, ball seated near the back hip/belly with soft pressure-ready hands for the deeper tailback's straight path. PROXY (solo) = downhill track, base, ball-vs-body position; the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: From the pistol, reach a downhill mesh on a balanced base with the ball seated near the back hip/belly and soft, pressure-ready hands, letting the deeper-aligned tailback press straight through the mesh point. (Camera judges the QB's downhill track, base, and ball position relative to his body; the exchange itself needs the RB.)

rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.

rows.fault_trigger: Head not neutral/level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral while eyes focus on the expected snap location + defensive alignment. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE focus = deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral while eyes focus on the expected snap location and maintain awareness of defensive alignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep behind center, hurting the window or timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] PISTOL depth: align at the prescribed depth behind center so the ball enters the optimal receiving window + preserves offensive timing. Pistol depth is SHORTER than shotgun (~3-3.5 yds vs ~5). Relative depth/alignment measurable; absolute needs a scale reference. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Align at the prescribed depth behind the center to ensure the football enters the optimal receiving window and preserves offensive timing.

rows.fault_trigger: Weight on the heels — delays downhill movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight balanced through mid-foot + balls of the feet for efficient reception + downhill movement. Weight = proxy (ankle-over-mid-foot is the signal). Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight remains balanced through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, supporting efficient reception and downhill movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Hands off the window, stiff, or poor finger spread. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
pose_landmarks: Right Elbow. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] PISTOL receiving window: hands comfortably in front of the torso at the anticipated snap location; fingers naturally spread + relaxed, elbows slightly flexed, a consistent window cushioning the ball into secure two-hand possession. Hand POSITION = pose-measurable; FINGER detail = needs the Hand landmarker. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hands positioned comfortably in front of the torso at the anticipated snap location — fingers naturally spread and relaxed with elbows slightly flexed, creating a consistent receiving window that cushions the football into secure two-hand possession.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong stagger/toe angle — unstable reception or inefficient first movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Proper stagger, toe angle, alignment — balanced snap reception + efficient first movement. Foot stagger/angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet maintain proper stagger, toe angle, and alignment for balanced snap reception and efficient first movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Knees locked or over-bent — loses explosive readiness.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knees slightly flexed — explosive athletic posture while preparing for the snap. Knee angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed to maintain an explosive athletic posture while preparing for the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide for balanced downhill movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Athletic base supporting downhill movement immediately following snap reception. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet establish an athletic base supporting downhill movement immediately following snap reception.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — poor support for run/pass.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Loaded hips, controlled chest, neutral spine — supports both downhill run action + passing mechanics. Pad level + posture measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain loaded hips, controlled chest, and neutral spine to support both downhill run action and passing mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders not square to the LOS.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders square to the LOS — efficient transition into the offensive concept. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain square to the line of scrimmage while supporting efficient transition into the offensive concept.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — immediate power generation after the catch. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso, allowing immediate power generation after the catch.

rows.fault_trigger: Wasted/choppy steps or feet out from under the body transitioning into the pass phase.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition from the fake into the pass footwork with efficient steps — feet under the body, throwing rhythm/balance/timing maintained. Footwork efficiency + step detection measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the fake into the designed pass footwork with efficient steps — feet under the body, maintaining balance, rhythm, and timing.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball exposed or dropped to one hand during the fake/transition. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand security through the fake and transition; ball protected against the body until committing to the throw (cross-cutting Ball Security). POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand security during the fake and transition — the ball remains protected against the body until the QB commits to the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Late/early or arrhythmic delivery from fake to throw. (On-schedule-for-route/defense judgment needs the route + defense; ball flight needs ball tracking — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Deliver on schedule per the route concept + defensive reaction, keeping rhythm from fake to throw. The QB's release TIMING/rhythm (fake→throw) is measurable from body motion; but 'on schedule for the route/defense' depends on the ROUTE + DEFENSE not in a solo clip — that judgment is deferred. Ball flight needs ball tracking. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver the football on schedule based on the route concept and defensive reaction while maintaining rhythm from fake to throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Eyes give away the fake or fail to transition to the read. (Eye gaze/reads not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Use eyes to influence defenders during the fake, then transition vision to the read/receiver progression while keeping body control. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/reads = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Use the eyes to influence defenders during the fake, then quickly transition vision to the defensive read and receiver progression while maintaining body control.

rows.fault_trigger: Half-hearted body commitment or pulling the ball early — no believable run picture. (Ball-presentation + eye parts need ball tracking / are gaze-deferred.)
pose_landmarks: Sternum. (Ball Position needs ball tracking; eyes = gaze deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Sell the run with full-body commitment — eyes, shoulders, hips, ball presentation replicate the run concept; don't pull the ball early; create a believable run picture. Pistol = downhill full-body sell. BODY sell (shoulder/hip/posture + not-pulling-early timing) = measurable; BALL presentation = needs BALL TRACKING; eyes/gaze = deferred. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sell the run by committing the entire body — eyes, shoulders, hips, and ball presentation replicate the intended run concept; avoid pulling the ball early, creating a believable run picture before transitioning to throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or over-rotate through the fake, hurting accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled shoulders through the fake, then rotate efficiently toward the target without opening early (which hurts accuracy). Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain controlled shoulders through the fake, then rotate efficiently toward the target without opening early.

rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed/bobbled snap or unbalanced/slow transition into the play-action footwork. (Finger/ball detail needs hand model / ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Right Knee. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — folded-in note] Snap received with proper timing/rhythm from cadence, body balanced, transitions smoothly into play-action footwork. Under center = hands under center; gun/pistol = clean catch (pistol prepares for downhill). Snap detail also folded into Stance. Timing/balance/transition measurable; finger + ball detail needs hand model / ball tracking. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the snap with proper timing and rhythm from cadence — body balanced — and transition smoothly into the designed play-action footwork.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips over-open early or fail to rotate through the throw, losing power/accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips controlled during the fake, then rotate efficiently through the throw for power + accuracy (pistol: keep hips underneath the body). Hip-line + rotation timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips controlled during the fake, then rotate efficiently through the throw to generate power and maintain accuracy.

rows.fault_trigger: Fails to reset into a loaded, aligned, throwing-ready posture after the fake.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Regain a throwing-ready posture — knees slightly bent, hips loaded, feet under the body, shoulders ready to align to the target. The reset-to-throw state (base + load + alignment) measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Regain a balanced throwing posture with feet underneath the body, hips loaded, knees slightly bent, and shoulders ready to align toward the target.

rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow (no lane) or too deep/drifting after the fake, breaking timing. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
pose_landmarks: Pelvis Center. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — RECOMMENDATION/relative] Maintain proper depth from the LOS after snap + fake (pistol: relationship from center + backfield action) — depth creates throwing lanes while preserving route timing. Relative depth/position measurable; absolute needs a scale. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain proper depth from the line of scrimmage after the snap and fake — depth creates throwing lanes while preserving route timing.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low, elbows flared, or away from the body before the mesh. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
