The ARM-EXTENSION point/geometry is measurable; the exact ball-release instant needs ball tracking. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ball releases at the optimal point above and slightly forward of the throwing shoulder, with arm extension and body alignment supporting accuracy.

rows.fault_trigger: Head drifts off the spine or destabilizes through the throw. (Actual eye gaze not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head stable over the spine; eyes on target throughout. Landmarks: head, neck, eye direction. Head STABILITY/orientation = measurable (head over spine); actual EYE gaze = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains stable over the spine; eyes stay focused on the target throughout the throwing sequence.

rows.fault_trigger: Elbow drops/disconnects or the arm loops — inefficient, inconsistent path. (Ball position itself needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Efficient overhand arm path; elbow stays connected to shoulder position; hand travels behind and through the ball. Landmarks: shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand (ball needs tracking). Arm-path geometry measurable; the BALL point needs ball tracking. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Throwing arm follows an efficient overhand path — elbow connected to shoulder position, hand traveling behind and through the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Hand cuts off early/across the body, or QB loses balance on the finish.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Throwing hand finishes toward the target; body decelerates naturally, maintaining balance + recovery. Landmarks: throwing hand, elbow, shoulders, hips, feet. Finish direction + deceleration + balance all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Throwing hand finishes toward the target; body decelerates naturally while maintaining balance and a recovery position.

rows.fault_trigger: Weight drifts or collapses, or force stays on the back leg — power leaks out of the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Force transfers back-leg→hips→target; lead leg stabilizes, no excessive drift/collapse. Landmarks: trail foot, lead foot, knees, hips, center of mass. MOTION/direction measurable; actual force is a proxy. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transfer force from the back leg through the hips into the target direction; the lead leg creates stability, preventing excessive drift or collapse.

rows.fault_trigger: Front shoulder opens early or shoulders tilt/dip through release — accuracy and power suffer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Front shoulder directed at target during loading; shoulders rotate AFTER hip initiation, stay level through release. Landmarks: lead shoulder, throwing shoulder, chest orientation. Shoulder-line angle + rotation timing. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Front shoulder stays directed toward the target during loading; shoulders rotate after hip initiation and remain level through release.

rows.fault_trigger: Wrong velocity/trajectory/location for the route. (Ball outcome + accuracy need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: and location need ball tracking plus the receiver/defender context.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — DEFERRED, BALL] Deliver with appropriate velocity, trajectory, location for the route/defense. Landmarks: release location, hand position, shoulder alignment, ball path. The BALL outcome (velocity/trajectory/location/accuracy) needs BALL TRACKING (+ target for accuracy). The body mechanics producing it are measurable via the other rows. Deferred.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver the football with appropriate velocity, trajectory, and location based on the route and defensive situation.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open before hips (out of sequence) or hips slide laterally — lost power and accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips INITIATE the sequence BEFORE shoulder rotation — pelvis rotates toward target, balanced, no lateral slide. Landmarks: left hip, right hip, pelvis angle, shoulders, spine. The hip-before-shoulder TIMING is a signature measurable signal. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips initiate the throwing sequence before the shoulders — pelvis rotates toward the target while maintaining balance and preventing lateral slide.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders lead instead of hips, or hips slide laterally — broken sequence, lost torque.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Pelvis initiates rotation toward target BEFORE shoulders; hips rotate aggressively, posture maintained, no lateral movement. Landmarks: left hip, right hip, pelvis angle. Hip-first timing + rotation measurable. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Pelvis initiates rotation toward the target before the shoulders — hips rotate aggressively while maintaining posture and preventing lateral movement.

rows.fault_trigger: Accuracy breaks down as velocity increases. (Velocity/accuracy/trajectory need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: and accuracy need ball tracking plus target context.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — DEFERRED, BALL] Maintain accuracy while generating increased velocity through rotational force. Landmarks: release point, hand position, ball trajectory. Velocity/accuracy/trajectory = BALL outcome, needs BALL TRACKING (+ target). Body mechanics producing it are in the other rows. Deferred.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain accuracy while generating increased velocity through rotational force.

rows.fault_trigger: Weak/narrow base or torso not stacked — can't generate or transfer rotational force.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Strong rotational base, feet connected to the ground, knees loaded, athletic hips, torso stacked over the lower body. Landmarks: feet, knees, hips, spine. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Strong rotational base — feet connected to the ground, knees loaded, hips athletic, torso stacked over the lower body.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open prematurely, spending the stored separation too early.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Front shoulder controls direction; upper body stays connected to hip rotation; shoulders avoid opening prematurely. Landmarks: lead shoulder, throwing shoulder. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Front shoulder controls direction while the upper body stays connected to hip rotation; shoulders avoid opening prematurely.

rows.fault_trigger: Arm fires before rotation (out of sequence) or elbow disconnects — arm-dominant, less velocity.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Arm accelerates AFTER rotational sequencing begins; elbow stays connected to shoulder movement; hand travels efficiently. Landmarks: shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand. Arm-path geometry + the after-rotation timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Arm accelerates after rotational sequencing begins — elbow stays connected to shoulder movement while the hand travels efficiently through the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Abrupt/unbalanced deceleration or hand finishes away from the target.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Decelerate naturally through rotation; throwing hand finishes toward target, balance maintained. Landmarks: hand, elbow, shoulders, hips. Finish + deceleration + balance measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Decelerate naturally through the rotation — throwing hand finishes toward the target while maintaining balance.

rows.fault_trigger: All-arm throw — no ground-up energy transfer through the chain.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Generate force through the feet, transfer energy UP the kinetic chain rather than relying on the arm. Landmarks: feet, ankles, knees, hips, center of mass. The kinetic-chain SEQUENCE/timing (ground→hips) is measurable; actual force is a proxy. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Generate force through the feet and transfer energy upward through the kinetic chain instead of relying only on the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips and shoulders open together (no separation) — no stored torque, arm-dominant throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] SEPARATION between hips and shoulders during loading — hips begin opening while shoulders stay closed to store rotational energy. Landmarks: hip angle, shoulder angle, torso rotation. This is THE separation signal: the ANGLE between hip-line and shoulder-line — one of the strongest measurable signals in all of throwing. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Create separation between hips and shoulders during loading — hips begin opening while shoulders remain closed to store rotational energy.

rows.fault_trigger: Torso disconnected from hip rotation or spine collapses — energy leak between lower and upper body.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Torso transfers energy from lower to upper body — chest follows hip rotation while spine alignment is maintained. Landmarks: spine, chest, shoulders, hips. Chest-follows-hip rotation timing + spine posture measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Torso transfers energy from the lower body into the upper body — chest follows hip rotation while maintaining spine alignment.

rows.fault_trigger: Early release (before full transfer) or release point drifts as velocity rises — inconsistency. (Exact ball point needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Ball releases AFTER maximum energy transfer (lower body→torso); release stays consistent despite increased velocity. Landmarks: shoulder, elbow, wrist (ball needs tracking). Arm-extension/release geometry + timing measurable; exact ball point needs tracking. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Ball releases after maximum energy transfer from the lower body through the torso; release stays consistent despite increased velocity.

rows.fault_trigger: Excessive side-sweep or looping in the arm path — inefficient, inconsistent sidearm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Arm travels efficiently through a lower HORIZONTAL path, no excessive side movement or looping. Landmarks: shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand. Arm-path geometry measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Arm travels efficiently through a lower horizontal path without excessive side movement or looping.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball misses the tight window or loses velocity. (Accuracy/velocity/window need ball tracking + a target — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: (Not pose-measurable — release point and ball path need ball tracking plus throwing-window context.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — DEFERRED, BALL] Deliver accurate throws through tighter windows while keeping velocity/control. Landmarks: release point, ball path. Accuracy/velocity/window = BALL outcome, needs BALL TRACKING (+ target). Body mechanics in the other rows. Deferred.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Deliver accurate throws through tighter throwing windows while maintaining velocity and control.

rows.fault_trigger: Arm-dominant throw with hips not initiating, or hips out of control on the lower slot.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Lower body still initiates force; hips rotate toward the target with control. Landmarks: hips, pelvis angle. Hip rotation + initiation timing measurable. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Lower body still initiates force production — hips rotate toward the target while maintaining control.

rows.fault_trigger: Over- or under-adjusting the torso angle, or losing posture/balance creating the lane.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Adjust BODY ANGLE to create the sidearm throwing lane while keeping posture + balance. Landmarks: spine angle, shoulders, hips. Torso/spine angle is directly measurable — this is the defining sidearm adjustment. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Adjust body angle to create the sidearm throwing lane while maintaining posture and balance.

rows.fault_trigger: Inconsistent arm slot or elbow disconnected from shoulder — erratic sidearm release.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent SIDEARM ANGLE; elbow position stays connected to shoulder movement, supporting the intended throwing lane. Landmarks: shoulder, elbow, wrist. THE defining sidearm signal: the arm-slot ANGLE (shoulder-elbow-wrist) — directly measurable, distinguishes sidearm from overhand. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a consistent sidearm angle — elbow position stays connected to shoulder movement and supports the intended throwing lane.

rows.fault_trigger: Release point varies from throw to throw at the sidearm slot — inconsistency. (Exact ball point needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Ball releases from a CONSISTENT sidearm position with proper timing/trajectory. Landmarks: elbow, wrist (ball needs tracking). Arm-position/release geometry + timing measurable; exact ball point needs tracking. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Football releases from a consistent sidearm position with proper timing and trajectory.

rows.fault_trigger: Excessive sideways lean or falling away from the target — lost power and accuracy.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transfer energy toward the target WITHOUT excessive sideways lean or falling away. Landmarks: feet, hips, spine. Direction of transfer + lean angle measurable (falling-away is a torso-angle signal). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transfer energy toward the target while avoiding excessive sideways lean or falling away from the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Base doesn't support the lower slot, or feet/hips/shoulders disconnect from the target line.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Athletic base supporting a LOWER release angle; feet, hips, shoulders stay connected toward the target. Landmarks: feet, knees, hips, shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Athletic throwing base that supports a lower release angle — feet, hips, and shoulders remain connected toward the target.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders drift off the target line while dropping to the lower slot.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders stay aligned with the target while supporting the lower arm slot. Landmarks: lead shoulder, throwing shoulder. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain aligned with the target while supporting the lower arm slot.

rows.fault_trigger: Poor finger control at the altered angle — wobble or off-line rotation. (Finger detail needs the hand model; rotation needs ball tracking.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker; Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] Fingers control ball rotation/direction despite the altered arm angle. Landmarks: wrist, hand, ball. Wrist POSITION = pose; FINGER control = needs the Hand landmarker; ball rotation needs ball tracking. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Fingers control the football's rotation and direction despite the altered arm angle.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.
rows.fault_trigger: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Knees crossing (karaoke-style) rather than the feet gliding past. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Weight shifting forward onto the front foot, preventing a clean load. Toes pointing backward or knees swinging wide off the linear path. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or wasted movement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet glide low to the ground — low vertical oscillation of the ankles/hips, ground contact maintained, minimal heel contact. The ONE designed crossover is foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. The designed crossover step is a FOOT crossing past foot while the knees stay on a linear path; the knees do not cross over one another as in a karaoke drill. Base stays wide enough to hold balance and weight stays centred, not forward on the front foot.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — stay low, don't bounce.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong step count or inconsistent rhythm through the three steps. Crossover missing, or occurring on the wrong step (it belongs on the second). Steps too long or too choppy so the rhythm no longer matches the route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the correct THREE-step progression with consistent rhythm — each step builds controlled depth while keeping throwing posture. Contains ONE crossover, on the second step. Step count, crossover count + position, and rhythm all measurable (this is the signature 3-step timing, ~1.2-1.4s under center). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the correct three-step progression with consistent rhythm — each step building controlled depth while maintaining throwing posture. The drop contains ONE crossover step: the second step crosses to turn the hips toward the target and gain separation, with the third step planting to establish a balanced throwing base.

rows.fault_trigger: Rushed, paused, or arrhythmic drop tempo.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent timing from snap through the final step — smooth, no pauses or rushed movement. Tempo/rhythm measurable (the ~1.2-1.4s 3-step signature). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent timing from snap reception through the final step — smooth, without pauses or rushed movement.

rows.coaching_cue: Two hands on it — relaxed, not loose.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball drops off the chest or elbows flare during the drop. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.) Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position.
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand ball security from snap through the drop — ball near the chest, elbows controlled, ready to transition to the throw. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand football security from the snap through the drop — ball near the chest with elbows controlled and ready to transition into the throwing motion. Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

rows.fault_trigger: Head unstable/bobbing or eyes drop during the drop. (Eye progression not pose-measurable — deferred.) Head bouncing, dipping, or rocking through the drop; upper body unstable, degrading spatial awareness and balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Vision downfield throughout the drop — head stable while eyes progress through coverage. Head STABILITY/orientation measurable; actual EYE progression = deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain vision downfield throughout the drop — head stable while the eyes progress through the defensive coverage. Head stays stable and level over the spine throughout the drop — no bouncing, dipping, or rocking of the upper body, which costs spatial awareness and balance.

rows.fault_trigger: Slow/unbalanced or mistimed transition from stance into the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition from the under-center stance into the drop efficiently after securing the snap — first movement controlled, balanced, timed with throwing rhythm. Transition timing + balance measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition from the under-center stance into the drop efficiently after securing the snap — first movement controlled, balanced, and timed with the QB's throwing rhythm.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop for immediate throwing.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Athletic throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an athletic throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep for the three-step concept. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Reach the designed three-step depth with throwing posture — depth allows timing + separation from the rush. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the designed three-step depth while maintaining throwing posture — depth allows proper timing and separation from the rush.

rows.fault_trigger: Overstriding or inconsistent stride length, hurting balance. Steps too long or too choppy, so the rhythm of the drop no longer matches the pass route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent stride length for a three-step drop — create depth without overstriding or losing balance. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent stride length appropriate for a three-step drop — creating depth without overstriding or losing balance. Stride length stays consistent and matched to the route’s timing — neither over-long nor choppy.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or tilt during the drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders controlled + level throughout the drop — avoid opening early, keep the ability to rotate efficiently to the target. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain controlled and level throughout the drop — avoiding early opening while maintaining the ability to rotate efficiently toward the target. Shoulders stay level and controlled through the drop. The front shoulder neither collapses nor over-rotates — either turns the hips prematurely and blinds vision to one side.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips drift out from under the body or misalign during the drop. Back hip locked or tight through the crossover, preventing clean weight transfer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips under the body + aligned throughout — maintain lower-body positioning for efficient throwing power. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain underneath the body and aligned throughout the drop — maintaining lower-body positioning to generate efficient throwing power. Hips stay loose and mobile through the crossover so weight can transfer cleanly into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — feet drift or require extra steps before the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Correct plant position at the top of the drop — feet stop efficiently, allowing immediate transfer into the throw. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable (key to the 3-step). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish the correct plant position at the top of the drop — feet stop efficiently, allowing immediate transfer into the throwing motion.

rows.fault_trigger: Finishes off-balance or not throwing-ready at the top of the drop. Weight stuck on the back foot at release, so the throw lacks ground force and becomes all arm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Finish in a balanced throwing posture — feet under the body, hips loaded, shoulders aligned, ready to deliver. The complete throwing platform measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Finish the drop in a balanced throwing posture — feet underneath the body, hips loaded, shoulders aligned, and ready to deliver the football. Weight transfers off the back foot into the throw, generating ground force rather than leaving the throw to the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Slow, misdirected, or off-balance first step.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Quick, efficient first step in the designed direction — proper spacing, balance, body ready to throw. First-step direction/quickness measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a quick, efficient first step in the designed direction — creating proper spacing while maintaining balance and staying ready to throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Finishes off-balance or not throwing-ready at the top of the drop. Weight stuck on the back foot at release, so the throw lacks ground force and becomes all arm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Finish in a balanced throwing position — feet under the body, hips loaded, shoulders aligned, immediate ability to deliver. The complete throwing platform measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Finish in a balanced throwing position — feet underneath the body, hips loaded, shoulders aligned, and immediate ability to deliver the football. Weight transfers off the back foot into the throw, generating ground force rather than leaving the throw to the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Athletic throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet under the body to support immediate throwing mechanics. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain an athletic throwing base at the completion of the drop — feet underneath the body to support immediate throwing mechanics.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — stay low, don't bounce.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong step count or inconsistent rhythm/spacing through the five steps. Fewer or more than two crossovers, or crossovers on the wrong steps. Steps too long or too choppy so the rhythm no longer matches the route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the correct FIVE-step progression with consistent rhythm + spacing — each step builds controlled depth while keeping throwing posture. Contains TWO crossovers. Step count, crossover count + position, and rhythm all measurable (~1.8-2.0s 5-step signature). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the correct five-step progression with consistent rhythm and spacing — each step building controlled depth while maintaining throwing posture. The drop contains TWO crossover steps, which clear the pocket and build the depth the intermediate route concepts need, finishing on a balanced plant.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.

Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Weight shifting forward onto the front foot, preventing a clean load. Toes pointing backward or knees swinging wide off the linear path. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Heavy heel contact or movement that disrupts timing.

The TWO designed crossovers are foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. The two designed crossover steps are FOOT crossing past foot while the knees stay on a linear path; the knees do not cross over one another as in a karaoke drill. Base stays wide enough to hold balance and weight stays centred, not forward on the front foot.

rows.coaching_cue: Two hands on it — relaxed, not loose.

pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand ball security from snap through the drop — ball tight to the chest, elbows controlled, until transitioning to the throw. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand football security from snap reception through the drop — ball tight to the chest with elbows controlled until transitioning into the throwing motion. Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or tilt during the drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + controlled throughout the drop — avoid early opening while keeping the ability to rotate efficiently into the throw. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and controlled throughout the drop — avoiding early opening while maintaining the ability to rotate efficiently into the throw. rows.fault_trigger: Head unstable/bobbing or eyes drop during the drop. (Eye progression not pose-measurable — deferred.) Head bouncing, dipping, or rocking through the drop; upper body unstable, degrading spatial awareness and balance.

rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain disciplined vision downfield throughout the drop — head stable while eyes progress through defensive coverage. rows.fault_trigger: Inconsistent stride length across the five steps, hurting depth/balance. Steps too long or too choppy, so the rhythm of the drop no longer matches the pass route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent stride length through the five-step drop — proper depth while keeping balance + throwing readiness. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent stride length throughout the five-step drop — creating proper depth while maintaining balance and throwing readiness. Stride length stays consistent and matched to the route’s timing — neither over-long nor choppy.

rows.fault_trigger: Weak/misdirected first step or wasted movement initiating the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Efficient first step creating depth while keeping balance + shoulders controlled — initiates the drop without wasted movement. First-step measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.fault_trigger: Rushed, paused, or disconnected drop tempo.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent timing from snap through the final step — smooth + connected, no rushing or pausing. Tempo/rhythm measurable (~1.8-2.0s). Needs motion pipeline.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — requires extra recovery steps before the throw.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Correct plant position at the completion of the five-step drop — plant foot creates a balanced throwing posture without extra recovery steps. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.fault_trigger: Slow/unbalanced or mistimed transition into the five-step drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition smoothly from the under-center stance into the five-step drop after securing the snap — controlled, balanced, timed with the passing concept. Transition timing + balance measurable. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Reach the designed five-step depth with throwing posture — proper separation from the LOS + allows route development. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips drift out from under the body or misalign during the drop. Back hip locked or tight through the crossover, preventing clean weight transfer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned under the body during the drop — maintain lower-body positioning for efficient throwing power. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain aligned underneath the body during the drop — maintaining lower-body positioning to generate efficient throwing power. Hips stay loose and mobile through the crossover so weight can transfer cleanly into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Head unstable or eyes drop during the drop. (Eye progression not pose-measurable — deferred.) Head bouncing, dipping, or rocking through the drop; upper body unstable, degrading spatial awareness and balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Downfield vision throughout the drop while progressing through reads — head controlled, no unnecessary movement. Head STABILITY/orientation measurable; actual EYE progression = deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain downfield vision throughout the drop while progressing through reads — head controlled without unnecessary movement. Head stays stable and level over the spine throughout the drop — no bouncing, dipping, or rocking of the upper body, which costs spatial awareness and balance.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — stay low, don't bounce.
rows.fault_trigger: Wrong step count, drifting, or lost posture across the seven steps. Fewer or more than three crossovers, or crossovers on the wrong steps. Steps too long or too choppy so the rhythm no longer matches the route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Complete the SEVEN-step progression with consistent rhythm + spacing — create depth without drifting or losing throwing posture. Contains THREE crossovers, extending the five-step pattern with an additional crossover and plant sequence. Step count, crossover count + position, and rhythm all measurable (~2.5-2.7s). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the seven-step progression with consistent rhythm and spacing — creating depth without drifting or losing throwing posture. The drop contains THREE crossover steps, extending the five-step pattern with an additional crossover and plant sequence for deep, long-developing route concepts.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow/wide at the top of the deeper drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Stable athletic base after completing the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain a stable athletic base after completing the drop — feet positioned to support immediate throwing mechanics.

rows.coaching_cue: Two hands on it — relaxed, not loose.
rows.fault_trigger: Ball drops off the chest or elbows flare during the longer drop. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.) Dropping to one hand on the ball. Arms stiff, or flailing/crossing the body’s midline, forcing the torso to overwork and sapping rotational energy. Ball drifting off a consistent carriage position.
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure two-hand carriage throughout the seven-step drop — ball protected against the body until the throwing phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; Ball Position needs BALL TRACKING. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain secure two-hand football carriage throughout the seven-step drop — ball protected against the body until the throwing phase begins. Both hands stay securely on the ball throughout the drop. Arms and hands stay relaxed but controlled — not stiff, not so loose that the ball drifts and body position goes with it. Hands do not cross the body’s midline.

rows.fault_trigger: Inconsistent stride length across the seven steps, hurting balance at depth. Steps too long or too choppy, so the rhythm of the drop no longer matches the pass route.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Controlled, consistent stride length through the seven-step progression — maintain balance at greater depth. Stride length measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain controlled, consistent stride length throughout the seven-step progression — allowing the QB to maintain balance at greater depth. Stride length stays consistent and matched to the route’s timing — neither over-long nor choppy.

rows.fault_trigger: Slow/unbalanced or mistimed transition into the seven-step drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Transition smoothly from the under-center stance into the seven-step drop — controlled while creating additional depth for deeper-developing concepts. Transition timing + balance measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Transition smoothly from the under-center stance into the seven-step drop after securing the snap — controlled movement creating additional depth for deeper developing concepts.

rows.fault_trigger: Slowing before the plant, arriving early, or arrhythmic tempo.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Consistent tempo through all seven steps — smooth, no slowing before the final plant or arriving early. Tempo/rhythm measurable (~2.5-2.7s). Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain consistent tempo through all seven steps — smooth, without slowing before the final plant or arriving early.

rows.fault_trigger: No clean plant — poor plant-foot location or unbalanced at the top of the drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Reach the top of the drop with proper plant-foot location + balanced position — allowing immediate transition into the throw. Plant-foot detection + timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the top of the drop with proper plant foot location and balanced body position — allowing immediate transition into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips drift out from under the body or misalign during the drop. Back hip locked or tight through the crossover, preventing clean weight transfer.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips under the body + aligned throughout — maintain lower-body positioning for efficient force transfer. Hip-line + position measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain underneath the body and aligned throughout the drop — maintaining lower-body positioning for efficient force transfer. Hips stay loose and mobile through the crossover so weight can transfer cleanly into the throw.

rows.fault_trigger: Incomplete platform — unbalanced feet, unloaded hips, or misaligned shoulders at the top of the drop. Weight stuck on the back foot at release, so the throw lacks ground force and becomes all arm.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Establish a complete throwing platform — balanced feet, loaded hips, aligned shoulders, proper weight transfer for the throw. The complete throwing platform measurable from pose. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a complete throwing platform — balanced feet, loaded hips, aligned shoulders, and proper weight transfer for the throw. Weight transfers off the back foot into the throw, generating ground force rather than leaving the throw to the arm.

rows.fault_trigger: Too shallow/deep for the seven-step concept. (Absolute depth needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partly RECOMMENDATION] Reach the proper seven-step depth with balanced throwing posture — protection space while preserving timing with deeper routes. Relative depth measurable; absolute needs a scale. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the proper seven-step depth while maintaining a balanced throwing posture — creating protection space while preserving timing with deeper routes.

rows.coaching_cue: Cut grass with your cleats — feet glide, knees don't cross.
rows.fault_trigger: Bouncing, high-stepping, or riding up on the toes instead of gliding. Knees crossing (karaoke-style) rather than the feet gliding past. Base narrowing so the body leans and loses balance. Weight shifting forward onto the front foot, preventing a clean load. Toes pointing backward or knees swinging wide off the linear path. Crossing at a speed that costs control. Wasted steps or excessive vertical movement in the deeper drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet glide low to the ground through the longer drop — low vertical oscillation of the ankles/hips, ground contact maintained, no wasted steps. The THREE designed crossovers are foot crossing past foot; knee separation must be maintained (knees not crossing, karaoke-style). Base width held, weight not forward on the front foot. Glide/bounce, knee separation, base width and crossover detection all measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet glide low to the ground throughout the longer drop — cleats cutting grass, staying in contact so a balanced throwing base is available immediately. The three designed crossover steps are FOOT crossing past foot while the knees stay on a linear path; the knees do not cross over one another as in a karaoke drill. Base stays wide enough to hold balance and weight stays centred, not forward on the front foot.

rows.fault_trigger: Weak drive step or lost balance/posture initiating the deeper drop.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Strong DRIVE step initiating depth while keeping balance + protecting throwing posture. First/drive-step measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute a strong drive step that initiates depth while maintaining balance and protecting the throwing posture.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders open early or tilt during the deeper drop. Shoulders opening to the field too early, letting defenders read the throw instantly. Front shoulder collapsing or over-rotating, turning the hips early and cutting off vision to one side.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + controlled through the longer drop — avoid opening early while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulder-line angle + open-timing measurable. Needs motion pipeline.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and controlled through the longer drop — avoiding early opening while preparing to rotate into the throw. Shoulders stay level and controlled through the drop. The front shoulder neither collapses nor over-rotates — either turns the hips prematurely and blinds vision to one side.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) and hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, with no lateral tilt or rotation - confirming a square, symmetric base under center. NOTE: this checks squareness only; it cannot confirm true weight distribution (a separate Draft proxy elsewhere), and proximity to the snap exchange is not measurable without the Center in frame.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Set up in a balanced, parallel stance under center, keeping your weight perfectly symmetrical and your hands pressed tightly into the exchange pocket.

rows.fault_trigger: Clicking Heels. Turning around so tightly that your feet trip over each other. A sloppy first pivot slows your lateral velocity, letting an edge rusher hit you instantly.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a sharp ~90-degree open-gate pivot, opening the hips directly toward the rollout path. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: On the snap, execute an immediate open-gate pivot (opening your hips 90 degrees directly toward your rollout path) and take a violent, deep escape stride sideways.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Sprint intensity proxy: horizontal (lateral) displacement of Pelvis Center per frame, tracked continuously through the sprint. Coaching target: sustained high displacement-per-frame with no deceleration, consistent with '100% sprint velocity.' NOTE: this reports a RELATIVE displacement rate only - an absolute speed figure needs a real-world scale reference (player height capture, still an open decision) and a known frame rate; until then only relative comparisons (e.g. against this player's own top-speed baseline) are meaningful, not a universal threshold. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Because there is no ball fake, the deception is pure speed. Bring the ball tightly to your chest with both hands, drop your chin, and sprint horizontally at 100% velocity to outrun the unblocked edge defender.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Direct the Foot. Planting with your toe still pointed toward your deep drop track. This causes you to drift endlessly toward the sideline, completely shrinking your throwing window and running out of bounds.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: As you reach a depth of 6-7 yards deep in the backfield, slam your outside foot into the turf, instantly pointing your toe down a linear, downhill track toward the line of scrimmage. This foot serves as your steering rudder to stop your backward drift.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield first to locate your targets. Square your shoulders to your throw, snap your wrist, and deliver the ball while moving downhill to maximize pass velocity.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Squareness: the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) and hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) should both read as roughly horizontal in the front-view image plane, with no lateral tilt or rotation - confirming a square, symmetric base under center. NOTE: this checks squareness only; it cannot confirm true weight distribution (a separate Draft proxy elsewhere), and proximity to the snap exchange is not measurable without the Center in frame.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Establish a perfectly square, parallel base under the center. Ride your hands securely under the center's hips with your weight evenly distributed on the balls of your feet.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - NEEDS MOTION] Hip-line rotation: angle between the hip-line (Left Hip to Right Hip) orientation at the snap frame and its orientation ~10-15 frames later. Coaching target: a violent ~180-degree reverse-pivot, turning the back toward the line of scrimmage. NOTE: camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the ball and execute a violent reverse-pivot off your lead foot. Take an aggressive, deep crossover drop step away from the line of scrimmage, pointing your back toward the line to start your track toward the fake running back.

rows.fault_trigger: Staring Downfield. Keeping your eyes up and looking downfield during the mesh. If you don't commit your vision and head to the fake handoff, the linebackers will never bite on the run.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Torso flexion: angle between the Sternum-to-Pelvis-Center line and vertical, measured at the peak of the mesh point (side view). Coaching target: a clear forward bend at the waist, shielding the ball with the upper torso. NOTE: this measures torso BEND only, not 'vision committed to the mesh' - eye gaze is not pose-measurable, and head orientation is not a reliable substitute here since a bent-forward head position is ambiguous between watching the mesh and simply looking down. The coaching standard's real intent (linebackers can't read the fake) is only partially captured by this signal.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Seat the ball deeply into the running back's belly pocket with both hands. Ensure your head and eyes snap completely down into the fake mesh point, bending your waist slightly to shield the ball with your upper torso from the eyes of the linebackers.

rows.fault_trigger: Rounding the Corner. Drifting too deep or running a lazy, wide circle into the backfield. Failing to point your foot and drive flat along the edge allows an unblocked defensive end to hunt you down for a loss.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - CONVERGENCE] At the plant frame, compute the plant foot's heading vector (Heel to Foot Index, image plane) and compare it against the QB's actual movement heading (direction of hip-center/Pelvis-Center displacement over the following 5-10 frames). A clean plant shows these two vectors closely aligned; a late or flat-footed plant shows a real angular gap between where the foot pointed and where the body actually went. NOTE: this design deliberately never needs to know the play's intended direction - it only compares the foot's own signal against the body's own subsequent path, sidestepping the 'which way is the perimeter' problem. Camera angle (Front) is an assumption, not yet verified against real rollout footage.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Rip the ball out of the mesh at the last millisecond. Slam your outside foot hard into the turf, instantly pointing your toe and directing your final step down a wide, looping track toward the opposite edge. Hide the ball tightly against your back hip as you clear the edge.

rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT - PARTIAL] Shoulder squareness: angle of the shoulder-line (Left Shoulder to Right Shoulder) relative to horizontal in the front-view image plane, at the release frame. Coaching target: shoulders read as square/horizontal, indicating the torso is facing the target rather than still rotated from the preceding footwork. NOTE: this assumes the target/throw direction is roughly toward the camera (a front-view assumption, not yet verified against real footage) - if the actual target is significantly off-angle from the camera, this signal alone cannot distinguish 'squared to a different target' from 'not squared at all.'
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Snap your head and eyes downfield to locate the target. Square your shoulders completely to the target, keep your front shoulder pointed down the field, and deliver an accurate pass while maintaining forward-running momentum.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to open toward the run, stepping off the designated track, or crossing/choppy steps that stop momentum or drift off the path. (The track's aiming point depends on the called run concept, which is not captured — the app reports the track / open angle but does not judge which is correct.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS MOTION | UNDER CENTER] Secure 'butt to gut', pivot/open toward the run, step on the designated track matching the RB path; eyes up on the read key. Footwork efficiency + open angle/track measurable from pose; the aiming point depends on the run concept (deferred) — report the track, don't judge it.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: After securing the snap (ball 'butt to gut' — both hands to the stomach/chest before any movement), pivot and open toward the direction of the run and step along the designated track that matches the running back's path — efficient steps, proper spacing, timing and balance, staying on the track — with the eyes up on the read key / defensive line and peripheral vision guiding the exchange. The toes point along the designated track for the called run (the aiming point varies by run concept).

rows.fault_trigger: Hesitation, rushing, or a broken rhythm in the QB's own steps and hands into the mesh. (Whether the exchange itself is synchronised with the running back needs the RB in frame; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No)] The QB's own step timing + rhythm into the mesh — smooth, unhurried, matching the designed track/tempo. Measurable from pose (the QB's own body); the two-player synchronisation with the RB needs the RB in frame (deferred).
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Execute the QB's own footwork and hands into the mesh with smooth, unhurried timing and rhythm — no hesitation or rushing on the way to and through the exchange, matching the designed track and tempo. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own step timing and rhythm into the mesh; the two-player synchronisation with the running back needs the RB in frame.)

rows.fault_trigger: Drifting off the designated track or mesh position, breaking timing/spacing/blocking angles. (Under center the handoff is at the mesh, not depth-based; absolute distance needs a scale reference.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY | UNDER CENTER] Under center the exchange is at the mesh off the LOS, not depth-based — hold the designated track + mesh position for timing/spacing/blocking angles. Relative track/position measurable from pose; absolute distance needs a scale reference.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Under center, the exchange happens at the mesh right off the line of scrimmage, so depth is not the governing relationship — hold the designated track and mesh position (rather than a fixed backfield depth) so timing, spacing, and blocking angles are preserved.

rows.fault_trigger: Pulls away early, releases to one hand, or exposes the ball before the RB secures it. (Ball position + possession need ball tracking + the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Two-hand control until the RB clearly secures possession — don't pull away early or expose the ball during the exchange. POSE PROXY = hands-together/high; FULL confirmation needs BALL TRACKING + the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain two-hand control until the RB has secured possession — do not pull away early or expose the football during the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Eyes tip the play or disrupt the exchange. (Eye gaze/discipline not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Appropriate eye discipline for the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange / tipping the play. Head ORIENTATION measurable; actual EYE gaze/discipline = deferred (not pose-measurable). Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Maintain appropriate eye discipline based on the run concept — eyes support deception without interfering with the exchange mechanics.

rows.fault_trigger: Ball loose/low or away from the torso approaching the exchange. (Ball position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PROXY] Secure the ball with two hands — throwing hand back half, off-hand front half — tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase. POSE PROXY = hands-together/height/elbow-tuck; ball position needs BALL TRACKING. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the football with two hands — throwing hand controls the back half, off-hand secures the front — ball tight to the chest/torso until the exchange phase.

rows.fault_trigger: An off-track approach to the mesh, poor body position or balance, or the ball not presented into the running path. (Mesh quality itself — the running back securing the ball — needs the RB and ball tracking; not judged from a solo clip.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL (retiered from No) | UNDER CENTER] Off the LOS, reach the mesh on the correct track; present the ball into the running path; keep body position/balance. PROXY (solo) = the QB's own track, reach motion, ball-vs-body position; the RB securing the exchange needs the RB + ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Reach the designed mesh point right off the line of scrimmage on the correct track, presenting the ball with both hands into the running path while keeping body position and balance. (What the camera can judge is the QB's own track, reach, and ball position relative to his body; whether the running back secures the exchange needs the RB in frame.)

rows.fault_trigger: Hips open early or drift off the exchange path, exposing the ball / hurting balance.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips aligned with the exchange path, kept square + underneath the body to support balance/efficient movement; avoid early opening that exposes the ball. Hip-line + position measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Keep hips aligned with the exchange path, square and underneath the body to support balance — avoid early opening that exposes the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Poor placement — wrong height/angle/firmness or misaligned with the RB's pocket. (Fully needs ball tracking + the RB — not measurable solo.)
pose_landmarks: Ball Position. (Ball Position needs ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — FULLY DEFERRED, BALL + RB] Place the ball into the pocket created by the RB's arms/body — correct height, angle, firmness, nose/tip matching the RB's carry technique; stays aligned/secure until the RB completes possession. PURELY ball + the RB's arms — the MOST ball/2-person-dependent measurement in the QB catalogue. NOT measurable solo. Needs BALL TRACKING + RB. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Place the football into the pocket created by the RB's arms and body — correct height, angle, and firmness, with nose/tip placement matching the running back's carry technique.

rows.fault_trigger: Stops/stands up or loses balance instead of continuing the designed carry-out action. (Exchange-completion part needs the RB.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection action. The CONTINUATION action (QB's own body + balance) = measurable from pose (and reuses Bootleg/Play-Action rows). The exchange completion itself needs the RB. Partial. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Complete the exchange with proper follow-through — maintain balance and continue the designed carry-out, fake, boot, or protection responsibility.

rows.fault_trigger: Early/over-rotation of the shoulders, exposing the ball or disrupting placement.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders positioned to support the exchange + give the RB a clear running path; controlled, avoiding early/unnecessary rotation that exposes the ball or disrupts placement. Shoulder-line angle + rotation-timing measurable from pose. FORMATION-INDEPENDENT.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Position shoulders to support the exchange while maintaining body control and allowing the RB a clear running path — avoid early/unnecessary rotation.

rows.fault_trigger: Mistimed or bobbled snap, hands not seated under center, or an unbalanced entry into the exchange. (Hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL | UNDER CENTER] Hands under center, ball 'butt to gut' secured immediately; timing/rhythm, body balanced into the exchange. Timing/balance/posture measurable from pose; hand/ball detail needs the hand model / ball tracking.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Receive the snap from under center — hands seated under the center, the ball delivered 'butt to gut' and immediately secured with both hands to the stomach/chest — with proper timing and rhythm, body balanced and prepared to execute the exchange.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips unloaded/too high or spine rounded — not compact/balanced for the snap.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips loaded, chest upright, spine neutral — body compact + balanced preparing to receive the snap. Pad level (how loaded/low) + posture measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain loaded with the chest upright and spine neutral — the body remains compact and balanced while preparing to receive the snap.

rows.coaching_cue: Non-throwing foot back — load it, don't false step.
rows.fault_trigger: Feet square with no stagger, or the THROWING-side foot back instead of the non-throwing side — the back leg cannot load and the QB takes a false step forward to start the drop. Stagger too deep or too shallow to push off cleanly, or toe angle creating an unstable platform. (Judging which foot should be back requires the player's handedness.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Proper toe-to-heel relationship, stagger, and angle — stable exchange platform + efficient first step. Foot stagger/angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet are staggered so the NON-THROWING-side foot sits slightly back — left foot back for a right-handed QB, right foot back for a left-handed QB. The stagger loads the back leg, lets the QB push off efficiently, and starts the drop without a false step forward. Feet stay roughly shoulder-width apart (about armpit width) with knees comfortably flexed and a stable toe-to-heel relationship and toe angle. NOTE: the stagger direction depends on the player's throwing hand — handedness must be supplied by the app before this can be judged; without it, report the observed stagger without scoring it.

rows.fault_trigger: Shoulders tilted or not square to the LOS/center.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Shoulders level + square to the LOS/center — controlled snap exchange + efficient transition. Shoulder-line angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Shoulders remain level and square to the line of scrimmage and center, allowing a controlled snap exchange and efficient transition into the play.

rows.fault_trigger: Weight on the heels or rocking forward/backward, delaying movement. (Force is a proxy via ankle/COM position.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — partial force proxy] Weight centered through the mid-foot + balls of the feet for explosive post-snap movement, no rocking forward/backward. Weight = proxy (pose can't measure force; ankle-over-mid-foot + no rocking is the signal). Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Weight centered through the mid-foot and balls of the feet, allowing explosive movement immediately after the snap without rocking forward or backward.

rows.fault_trigger: Hands not seated under center, poor palm/finger relationship, or elbows flared — muffed/insecure snap. (Finger detail needs the hand model.)
pose_landmarks: Right Elbow. (Thumb/finger points need the Hand landmarker.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — NEEDS HAND MODEL] UNDER CENTER hand placement: bottom hand directly beneath center, palm UP, top hand covering; fingers naturally spread + relaxed for a broad target; wrists relaxed, elbows close to cushion the snap + immediately secure the ball. Hand POSITION (wrist/elbow) = pose-measurable; FINGER spread/palm detail = needs the Hand landmarker. THIS is the key under-center-specific row (differs from shotgun window). Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Bottom hand directly beneath the center with palm facing upward, top hand covering — fingers naturally spread and relaxed for a broad receiving target, wrists relaxed and elbows close to cushion the snap and immediately secure the football.

rows.fault_trigger: Base too narrow or too wide for a balanced exchange platform.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Feet ~shoulder-width apart — balanced athletic base supporting efficient snap reception + immediate movement. Base width measurable relative to shoulders. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Feet approximately shoulder-width apart — roughly under the armpits — establishing a balanced athletic base that supports efficient snap reception and immediate movement after the exchange, with knees comfortably flexed and weight balanced on the balls of the feet.

rows.fault_trigger: Hips rotated/off-square or not underneath the torso.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Hips square underneath the torso — efficient force transfer following the snap. Hip-line + position measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hips remain square underneath the torso, allowing efficient force transfer immediately following the snap.

rows.fault_trigger: Head tilted/dropped or chin not level. (Actual eye focus not pose-measurable — deferred.)
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT — PARTIAL] Head neutral, chin level; disciplined pre-snap focus while preserving posture + awareness. Head ORIENTATION/level measurable; actual EYE focus = deferred. Partial.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Head remains neutral with the chin level — eyes maintain disciplined pre-snap focus while preserving proper body posture and awareness.

rows.fault_trigger: Knees locked straight or over-bent — loses athletic readiness.
rows.measurable_signal: [DRAFT] Knees slightly flexed — athletic posture supporting a stable exchange + efficient movement. Knee angle measurable. Size-independent.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Knees remain slightly flexed, creating an athletic posture that supports a stable exchange and efficient movement after possession.

rows.fault_trigger: Failing to Clear the Center. Whipping around too fast before completely securing the snap, resulting in an immediate center-exchange fumble.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Secure the snap completely from the center before initiating any rotational movement.

rows.fault_trigger: "Floating" Away From the Line. Drifting backward into the backfield while running laterally, which closes down the pitch angle and lets one defender tackle both the QB and the RB.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Sprint laterally along the line of scrimmage, aggressively riding the line rather than retreating.
Immediately open the hips by pivoting strictly 90 degrees toward the play-side perimeter.
Extend both arms down and out, utilizing a smooth, two-handed underhand scooping motion.

rows.fault_trigger: "Spinning the Ball". Trying to throw a spiral on a toss, which makes the ball highly unstable in the air and incredibly difficult for a moving running back to track and catch cleanly.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Flick the wrists dynamically upon release to create a natural, end-over-end tumble.
Place the pitch precisely 1 yard out in front of the running back's numbers so they can catch it in full stride.
Keep the chest pointing forward to actively threaten the defense as a runner, with the ball tucked securely with two hands near the chest.
Attack the outside shoulder of the unblocked read-key edge defender to force them to commit.

rows.fault_trigger: Staring Down the Target. Looking directly at the pitch man or shovel receiver early, alerting the linebackers and allowing them to jump the play.
rows.ideal_execution_standard: Hold the attack trajectory until the defender physically commits to your chest.
Extend the arms and deliver a crisp, one-handed thumb-down flick (Speed Option) or a soft, two-handed basketball chest pass (Interior Shovel).
